_comment: THE WHO ONE-VOICES, staged as a top-level directory ahead of becoming their own repository — the same arrangement as who-iris/, folio-assistant-sci/ and folio-assistant-core/. Owner, 2026-09-20: 'the 3 one-voices, should reference the 3 artefacts in the who-iris library, but the 3 one voices are derived from the cataloge and in their own repo/dir.' DERIVED FROM is the whole relation: each voice is read rule by rule out of one IRIS publication, every rule cites the page it came from, and the publication itself lives in who-iris. So this instance holds no corpus and declares no `library` — it declares VOICES, and every one of them resolves its evidence across the instance boundary. That cross-instance citation is what bean z7ev built and what r1lz predicted would be needed: 'a skill derived from a source text in another repo would cite evidence its own instance cannot resolve.' DECLARE ONLY WHAT EXISTS, per dh4f: `voices/` is the only entry because it is the only directory here.

assets.description: Cold start for work in this layer, and the one rule that governs it: a voice is DERIVED FROM a publication and is not the publication. Source text is never copied here — every rule cites `{instance, libraryId, sectionId}` across the boundary and carries its quote and page, which is what makes a voice auditable rather than asserted.

directories.description: Three `folio-voice/v1` profiles, one per WHO publication in the who-iris library. A voice is a set of editorial RULES, each carrying the quote it was read from and a citation naming `{ instance: 'who-iris', libraryId, sectionId }`. The instance is declared once per voice in `sources[]` and INHERITED by its rules rather than repeated on each — one fact in one place, since a voice pointing at one instance with a rule pointing at another is representable, meaningless, and nothing would catch it. `bun run check:voices` resolves every citation through the target instance's own declaration and keeps four failure kinds apart; `milnor` is NOT here, because it is read from a mathematics paper and belongs with the science layer (bean r1lz).
